findings.text: A DMA remapping unit descriptor keeps list membership for the global table, a reference to its firmware header, a register area start plus area extent, a pointer to device scope entries plus its count, a PCI segment identifier, three one-bit marks for ignored versus include-all versus graphics-dedicated handling, and a back pointer to the associated IOMMU instance.

PCI location is expressed as a three-part bus device function value. Hotplug notification carries a device reference, an event code, bus and segment identifiers, a nesting level, and a packed trailing array of those location values describing the path.

Traversal of the global remapping-unit list and of device scope arrays happens under RCU with a guard that is satisfied while the global remapping lock is held or while the system is still booting. Active-only variants skip entries marked ignored or empty device slots.

When the remapping feature is unavailable the public helpers collapse to constant outcomes: resource parsers succeed without effect, fault dumping and shutdown and detection do nothing, hotplug and scope notification and device add and remove report success, initialization reports missing device, and platform opt-in reports false.

The interrupt remapping entry is a sixteen-byte value with two halves. The low half selects among a shared view, a remapped view with destination handling, trigger and delivery controls, vector and destination identifier, and a posted view with urgency, vector and low part of a descriptor address. The high half carries source identity and verification fields, with a posted variant holding the high part of the descriptor address. A helper copies only the shared subset between entries.
The posted descriptor address split reserves twenty six low bits and thirty two high bits for its two halves.

Early bring-up exposes minimal hooks for boot snapshot capture, general trace initialization, early trace initialization, module initialization and enablement, module release, and freeing of init memory, allowing callers to invoke them unconditionally.

Register capture for traced functions is opaque to generic code; architecture code provides the concrete layout and conversion helpers. Accessors yield absence when no capture exists, otherwise expose the embedded machine registers, with separate hooks for partial views, performance fill, instruction pointer update, direct caller update, and stack pointer derivation.

A trace operation bundles a callback, an RCU-linked successor, flag bits, private data, a saved callback, optional per-operation and shared filter tables with prior table state, trampoline location and size, list membership, sub-operation list, a command handler and a managed peer, plus an optional direct-call target. Each hash object holds RCU-protected filter and notrace tables guarded for updates by a dedicated mutex.

Operation behavior is selected by single-bit flags covering enabled, dynamic, register saving and conditional register saving, recursion handling, stub, initialized, deleted, adding, removing, modifying, trampoline allocation, instruction-pointer modification, process filtering, RCU mode, trace-array association, permanence, direct calls, sub-operation and graph tracing, with an alias for argument saving.

The live operation chain and the filter tables are read under RCU without locks, while changes to filter expressions serialize on the per-hash regex mutex and lifecycle transitions use the adding removing and modifying marks.
Iteration starts from a list head through an RCU dereference and advances through successors until the dedicated list-end marker, so readers never block writers.

Each instrumented site keeps an address and a flag word whose high bits record enabled, register use, trampoline use, modification permission, disabled, direct, call-ops, touched and modified states while the low bits hold a reference count. Update actions choose among ignore, create call, modify call and create no-op, and record iteration can filter by filter set, notrace set, probe state, module scope, enabled state, touched state and address reporting.

Without dynamic tracing support, registration, filtering, address lookup, symbol resolution, direct-call management, hash counting, graph control, text reservation and location queries collapse to fixed failures or empty results, with filter file operations reporting unsupported device and lookup helpers reporting zero or negative status.

The stack-tracer nesting counter is per processor and must only be adjusted with preemption or interrupts already disabled, with a debug check warning otherwise; one build disables the checks entirely. Global tracing can be forced off and saved or restored around critical sections.

Reading an indexed kernel stack slot through a captured register set succeeds only when the slot stays on the same thread stack, otherwise zero is returned, and one build always returns zero. A jump marker is encoded in the low address bit in one build and absent in the other. Argument availability is always true when argument capture is supported, otherwise it depends on whether registers were captured.

Fixed numeric and address constants define a default hash width of ten bits, update and control bits for calls and function return tracing and sleeping permission, bug categories for init and patch stages, hook kinds for entry versus return, and dedicated caller addresses for normal, graph and register variants plus a zero graph trampoline.

Direct trampolines and graph hooks have build-dependent availability: direct caller setup may be empty, direct support flags and graph stub marks select stub versus live behavior, and return-address helpers either expose the caller address or collapse to zero.

Sharing of instruction-pointer modification is negotiated through enable-self, enable-peer and disable-peer commands handled by the operation command callback. Code patching distinguishes no-op initialization needs, no-op creation, call modification and failure paths.
Direct lookup entries pair a hash linkage with an instruction address and an associated direct target value.
